newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIS urges Germany not to deport Algerians home.
newsitem.headline: FIS urges Germany not to deport Algerians home.

text.p: The outlawed Algerian Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) accused Germany on Wednesday of agreeing to hand back Algerian exiles whose requests for political asylum had been turned down.
The FIS leadership in exile, in a statement received in Paris, said the exiles risked torture or death if they were sent back to Algeria.
It said Bonn had agreed that Algerian policemen would fly to Germany to bring home unsuccessful asylum seekers in what it described as "forced extradition".

"Such an agreement is contrary to human rights defended by German democracy...especially after Amnesty International confirmed widespread torture by Algerian authorities in its latest report," it said.

"We ask the German government to renounce this agreement and not expel Algerian asylum seekers to their home country as they would ineluctably suffer in their human dignity and face real danger for their life."

FIS was outlawed and its top leaders jailed after Algerian authorities scrapped 1992 elections it was poised to win. About 60,000 people have since been killed in violence between Moslem guerrillas and government forces.
